newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Hindu party breaks deadlock in key state.
newsitem.headline: India's Hindu party breaks deadlock in key state.

text.p: India's rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) said on Wednesday it had agreed with an influential party of lower-caste Hindus to form a government in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh.
India's most populous state has been ruled directly by New Delhi after inconclusive local elections in September last year failed to produce a clear majority for any one political group.

A BJP spokesman told Reuters that under Wednesday's agreement his party would allow the rival Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) to head the two-party coalition government for six months, followed by a six-month turn at the helm by the BJP.
"Every six months we will change the party to head the government," the spokesman said. "The first government will be headed by the BSP."

The BSP's decision to join hands with the BJP was seen as a major setback for the Congress party, which had ruled India for all but three years since independence from Britain in 1947 and derived its strength largely from Uttar Pradesh.
The BSP and the Congress had jointly fought the September elections to the 425-member state legislature.
"This news does not bode well for the BSP nor for Uttar Pradesh," a Congress official told Reuters. "This kind of opportunism is going to make politicians look like saleable commodities."
Sharad Yadav, working president of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's Janata Dal Party said the BJP-BSP alliance was an unholy tie up to grab power, the United News of India (UNI) reported.
The BJP-BSP pact followed protests in parliament by the BJP which has demanded the dismissal of Uttar Pradesh governor Romesh Bhandari, saying he was responsible for a jump in crime in the state.
The parliament is expected to debate the issue on Thursday.
The Congress party, which has also demanded Bhandari's dismissal, said on Wednesday it would not support the BJP in the vote on the governor's recall.

Some politicians said the collapse of relations between BSP and the Congress in Uttar Pradesh could also nudge the Congress closer to Deve Gowda whose United Front government it has reluctantly supported for nine months.
